answer: An agent network can curb Sybil attacks using memory-hard cryptographic puzzles. Nodes maintain identity by solving graph-traversal challenges, binding each execution thread to physical RAM. This builds a firm cedar threshold, forcing an adversary to dedicate scarce memory bus bandwidth per persona rather than spawning a dune of cheap virtual clones. However, continuous memory saturation exhausts battery life and excludes micro-agents unable to allocate gigabytes of RAM.
